findings.title: retroRunOp's error branch in cmdRetro is never exercised
findings.detail: cmd_retro.go:73-75 (`if err != nil { return fail(env.Stderr, exitError, err.Error(), "") }`) is new code with no test that drives it. None of the cmd_retro_test.go cases make writeRetroArtifacts/retroRunOp fail (e.g. by removing spec.md or corrupting finish/verify.json before `retro --rewrite`), so this fail path — including its message format and exit code — is untested. The pattern mirrors an already-exercised branch in cmd_next.go:1021-1022, which lowers the risk, but the new call site itself has no coverage.

findings.title: The generated-session-id path through cmdRetro's nextRun construction is untested
findings.detail: cmd_retro.go:61-64 wires `sessionID(env.Getenv)`'s `generated` bool into `nextRun.genID`. Every test in cmd_retro_test.go runs with `TAKT_SESSION` explicitly set (via finishRun's driver env `{"TAKT_SESSION": "S"}` or TestRetroRewriteTargetsARunByDir's own env map), so `generated` is always false. No test invokes `retro --rewrite` with TAKT_SESSION unset, so the genID=true branch of this new wiring — which affects what gets recorded in the session file for future takeover decisions — is never exercised for this command.
